The copy lands far from average exactly when the copied piece is still inside an open word, so it crosses 0.25 x max (peaks 1.0-3.6) on the second and later pieces of a word the tokenizer splits - words split into three or more pieces (zy|kl|ische 3.1, ku|bi|ato 2.9, nip|a 1.8-3.0, Zeph|yr|us 1.8-1.9, Shost|ak|ovich 2.0, hex IDs) and two-piece words with a short first piece (Bat|anes 1.0, typ|ische 1.6) - and on 16/16 non-English passages tested across Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari, Hebrew, Spanish and Afrikaans (1.1-3.1), while it sits at its floor (0.0-0.6) after a whole word or a word-final piece: on space-initial words and function words (' the', ' of', ' house', ' is'), word-final suffixes ('ungen', 'shita', ' tou', 'aet'), punctuation, newlines, and one repeated token (0.00); ordinary English prose of one-token words is active-weak (0.0-1.1, 14/16 sentences below the line, crossing about one sentence in seven, e.g. ' cat sat' 0.96 or ' rest for' 1.07), code is mixed (median 0.84, 3/8 above the line) and plain number lists mostly stay below (5/6, 0.0-1.0).
